name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,782

entries.clue: Compliments a Eurovision runner-up (15)

blocks.note: first definition: praise offered on a success
second definition: Cliff Richard's song, second in the 1968 Eurovision Song Contest

annotation.surface: A gracious nod to whoever came second in the song contest.
annotation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard's 'Congratulations' famously lost the 1968 Eurovision by a single point, so the song title and the praise are the same word.
annotation.definitionFit: Congratulations are compliments paid to someone on their success.

entries.clue: Where to keep artists' busts? (6,2,7)

blocks.note: the question asks for a piece of furniture that stores things
the surface wants painters; read it as people who draw
the surface wants sculpted heads; read it as the body's chests

annotation.surface: A sculptor wondering where to store the busts in the studio.
annotation.walkthrough: Busts look like sculptures and artists look like painters; read the artists as drawers and the busts as chests, and the bedroom furniture appears.
annotation.definitionFit: A whole-clue definition by pun: storage furniture, renamed as the place where drawers keep their chests.

entries.clue: Mark's home with writer's block (7)

blocks.note: a note is a mark, as in a mark of distinction
pad = informal word for one's home

annotation.surface: An author called Mark sitting at home, unable to write a word.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' pretends to be the creative paralysis; it is literally a block of paper for writing on.
annotation.definitionFit: A notepad is a block of paper a writer jots on.

entries.clue: President set free Green swapping sides? (9)

indicatorNotes.swapping sides: the sides are left and right: each word trades its L for R or its R for L

blocks.note: LOOSE (set free) with L (left) swapped for R (right)
VERT (heraldic green) with R (right) swapped for L (left)

annotation.surface: A president releasing a Green politician who has crossed the floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swapping sides' sounds like political defection; it means L and R change places. VERT is the heraldic word for green.
annotation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both US presidents.

entries.clue: Man has ringing in the ears leaving pub (5)

indicatorNotes.leaving: INN leaves the word, so it is taken out

annotation.surface: A man stumbling out of a noisy pub with his ears still ringing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface gives a cause and effect; in fact the pub is subtracted from the medical term.
annotation.definitionFit: Crosswords use 'man' for any man's name; Titus is one, like the Roman emperor or Shakespeare's Titus Andronicus.

entries.clue: Aryan rule overthrown in roughly 354 days (5,4)

indicatorNotes.overthrown: the letters are thrown over into a new order

annotation.surface: A regime toppled within a year of taking power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overthrown' fits the political surface so well that it hides its job as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a year counted in twelve moon cycles falls about eleven days short of the solar year.

entries.clue: Draw on nationalist symbol (5)

blocks.note: to toke is to draw on a joint

annotation.surface: An instruction to sketch over a nationalist emblem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw on' suggests pencilling on something; it is the smoker's inhale.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that stands for something else, as a small gift given as a mark of thanks.

entries.clue: Former head's term of endearment (3,4)

blocks.note: old = former, as in an old flame

annotation.surface: A retired headmaster's fond way of addressing people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Former head' reads as an ex-headteacher; BEAN is old slang for the head. Old bean is a dated, upper-class British form of address to a friend.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Old bean' is an affectionate way of addressing a friend.

entries.clue: Hospitality maybe something offered by stud farm? (7,8)

blocks.note: the hotel and restaurant trade, named here as one example of a sector
in breeding, a stallion's covering of a mare is called service, and a stud sells it as a trade

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a stud farm's welcome counts as hospitality.
annotation.walkthrough: Service is the breeding term for a stallion covering a mare, so a stud farm is literally in the service industry; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Hospitality is a sector of the economy selling services rather than goods.

entries.clue: Has table in auberge at Southwark (4,3)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits inside the following words

annotation.surface: Someone who has booked a table at a French-style inn in Southwark.
annotation.walkthrough: An auberge is a French inn and Southwark a district of south London, which makes the setting feel like a restaurant review.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to have a table is to be seated at a restaurant for a meal rather than dining at home.

entries.clue: Dear Ken's running around with less on (7)

indicatorNotes.running around: the letters run around into a new order

annotation.surface: A letter warning that Ken has been streaking about in fewer clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dear Ken' opens like a letter, which hides the fodder in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Wearing less is being more naked.

entries.clue: Letter about European Parliament's accommodation (5)

indicatorNotes.about: 'About' in its sense of 'around', so the spelt-out letter wraps round EP.

blocks.note: TEE is the letter T spelt out; it holds the next block

annotation.surface: A letter concerning where the European Parliament houses its members.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letter about' looks like correspondence on a topic; it is a spelt-out letter wrapped around EP.
annotation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent, a form of accommodation.

entries.clue: Calm surrounds opening of gala appeal about wildlife reserve (9)

indicatorNotes.surrounds: A thing that surrounds another encloses it, so SERENE is placed around G.
indicatorNotes.opening of: The opening of a word is where it begins, so its first letter is taken.
indicatorNotes.about: 'About' as in 'turn about', meaning face the other way, so IT is read backwards.

blocks.note: serene = calm; it takes G inside, SEREN-G-E

annotation.surface: A serene charity gala launching a fundraising drive for a wildlife reserve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' reads as a charity campaign, but here it is IT, the old slang for sex appeal.
annotation.definitionFit: The Serengeti in Tanzania is a vast national park and wildlife reserve.

entries.clue: What slave traders did heading off Nubians? (3,6)

indicatorNotes.heading off: the head, the first letter, comes off

annotation.surface: A grim question about how slavers dealt with Nubian captives.
annotation.walkthrough: The Nubians of the Nile valley are an ancient people, so they are one example of an old people; the question mark flags the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Nubians are a people of great antiquity, one example of an old people.

entries.clue: Aviator with pilot's case arranged to see singer (9)

indicatorNotes.case: the case of a word is its outside letters

annotation.surface: An aviator and his pilot's luggage organised so he can catch a concert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pilot's case' looks like luggage; it is the outside of the word pilot.
annotation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was a celebrated operatic tenor.

entries.clue: Spirit regularly distilled from green rice (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: Something done regularly happens at even intervals, so letters are picked at a steady step, every other one.
indicatorNotes.distilled from: the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

blocks.note: G r E e N r I c E: 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th letters

annotation.surface: A spirit made by distilling a green rice mash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' and 'distilled' conspire to suggest liquor; the spirit is a supernatural one, as in Aladdin's lamp.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a jinn, a supernatural spirit of Arabian folklore.

entries.clue: Minimalist composer has change of heart with ordinary musical effect (9)

indicatorNotes.has change of heart: the middle letter is changed, A to I

blocks.clueFragment: Minimalist composer has change of heart
blocks.note: GLASS (Philip Glass) with its central A changed to I
O = ordinary, as in O level

annotation.surface: A minimalist composer changing his mind about using a particular effect.
annotation.walkthrough: Philip Glass is the best-known minimalist composer; his 'change of heart' is literal, the middle letter swapped.
annotation.definitionFit: A glissando is a musical slide from one pitch to another.

entries.clue: Launch of TV dinners initially rejected (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of dinners
indicatorNotes.rejected: the whole is sent back, read in reverse

blocks.note: reversal indicator: what is rejected is sent back, so the chunks read in reverse

annotation.surface: A new line of TV dinners that shoppers turned down at launch.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a failed product; 'rejected' sends TUBED back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a performer's first appearance, or a product's first outing, is its launch.

entries.clue: Old footballer welcomes doctor and swallows drug for healing process (3,4)

indicatorNotes.welcomes: To welcome a guest is to take them in, so BEST takes DR inside.
indicatorNotes.swallows: What is swallowed goes inside, so BEST also takes E inside.

blocks.note: George Best, the Northern Ireland and Manchester United star; he holds the next two blocks, BE…ST

annotation.surface: A retired footballer ushering in a doctor and taking medicine to recover.
annotation.walkthrough: George Best was a famous footballer of the 1960s and 70s; both DR and E go inside him.
annotation.definitionFit: Bed rest is staying in bed to recover from illness.

entries.clue: Colour of Manx cat eaten by rats? (9)

indicatorNotes.Manx: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: rats are vermin; the word holds the next block, VERMI…N
LION, a big cat, without its tail

annotation.surface: A Manx cat devoured by rats, and the colour it left behind.
annotation.walkthrough: The Manx is a tailless breed from the Isle of Man, so 'Manx' tells you to dock the last letter; the cat is a lion, not a tabby.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one colour, the bright red of the pigment made from cinnabar.

entries.clue: Eluding exotic pet (7)

indicatorNotes.exotic: the letters are made strange, rearranged

annotation.surface: An exotic pet on the loose, evading capture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pet' sits like a noun for an animal; it is the verb, to pet or pamper.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to pet a child is to spoil or pamper them.

entries.clue: Italian contributes to aria duo composed for opera houses? (9)

indicatorNotes.contributes to: IT is added to the fodder
indicatorNotes.composed: the letters are put together in a new order

annotation.surface: An Italian composer adding to an aria duet written for the opera houses.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'composed' look like songwriting; it is the anagram signal. The question mark marks opera houses as examples of auditoria.
annotation.definitionFit: Opera houses are examples of auditoria, halls where audiences sit.

entries.clue: Headdress of Spanish relative worn by a queen (5)

indicatorNotes.worn by: TIA is worn around A R, so it goes outside

blocks.note: tía is Spanish for aunt; it holds the next block, TI…A

annotation.surface: An aunt's headdress, borrowed by a queen.
annotation.walkthrough: A garment worn by someone goes around them, so TIA wraps A R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the jewelled crown-like band worn by royalty and brides.

entries.clue: Cover entrance to lock? (5)

blocks.note: the surface reads it as guard; here, a garment worn over clothes
a canal lock has a paved platform at its mouth, with the same name as the garment

annotation.surface: A request to guard the doorway of a lock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door or keyhole; it is a canal lock, whose entrance has an apron.
annotation.definitionFit: An apron covers the front of one's clothes.

entries.clue: Holy man's upset by eviscerated Hindu (5)

indicatorNotes.eviscerated: the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

annotation.surface: A holy man distressed by a gruesome killing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eviscerated' is gory in the surface but just means gutted: keep the ends.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Sanskrit-derived name for a wandering ascetic who has renounced worldly life.

entries.clue: Exquisite requiem's abridged by worker (7)

blocks.note: ELEGY (a lament, a requiem) with the last letter cut

annotation.surface: A beautiful requiem shortened by some labourer.
annotation.walkthrough: An elegy is a mournful poem or song, close kin to a requiem.
annotation.definitionFit: Elegant means exquisite, refined in style.

entries.clue: Covering letter enclosing lock of hair (7)

blocks.note: a ring covers or encircles, as a ring round a finger
a letter is one who lets out property

annotation.surface: A covering letter with a lock of hair tucked inside as a keepsake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covering letter' reads as the note sent with a job application; the landlord sense of letter, someone who lets, is the crossword standby.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a long curl of hair hanging down.

entries.clue: Job with Buffalo Bill involving me and Miranda? (9,6)

indicatorNotes.involving: To involve something is to include it, so CODY takes ME inside.

blocks.note: William Cody, Buffalo Bill; he holds the next block, CO…DY

annotation.surface: A job in a Wild West show alongside Buffalo Bill, me and a woman called Miranda.
annotation.walkthrough: Miranda is Miranda Hart's BBC sitcom; the question mark flags it as an example. 'Miranda' looks like another cast member.
annotation.definitionFit: Miranda was a BBC situation comedy, one example of the genre.
